statement: The registry accepts exactly the categories volume, mass and temperature, and loads only the requested category's plugin on first use, leaving the other categories unloaded.

faults.description: The valid category list drops temperature, so a valid category is rejected with UnknownCategory.
The first request for any category eagerly loads every other category's plugin too.
faults.replace:
const key = category as Category;
  for (const c of CATEGORIES) if (c !== key && !loaded.has(c)) loaded.set(c, import(`./plugins/${c}.ts`) as Promise<Plugin>);

statement: Volume conversions use the fixed ratios (1 l = 1000 ml, 1 cup = 240 ml, 1 tbsp = 15 ml, 1 tsp = 5 ml) and return a number rounded to 2 decimal places, half away from zero.

faults.description: A cup is treated as 250 ml instead of 240 ml, so 2 cup to ml returns 500.

The volume plugin returns the result as a string (toFixed(1)) instead of a number rounded to 2 decimals. The change runs as JavaScript but fails the strict TypeScript check, because the function is declared to return number.

statement: Mass conversions use 1 kg = 1000 g, 1 lb = 453.6 g and 1 oz = 28.35 g, converting from the source unit to the target unit and rounding to 1 decimal place.

faults.description: An ounce is treated as 28 g instead of 28.35 g, so 1 lb to oz returns 16.2 instead of 16.0.
Source and target units are swapped in the call, so the conversion runs in the inverse direction without throwing.

statement: Absolute temperatures convert with the 9/5 factor plus the 32 offset, deltas use the scale factor only with no offset, and only absolute inputs below absolute zero fail with BelowAbsoluteZero, so deltas have no lower bound.

faults.description: The Celsius-to-Fahrenheit offset is 30 instead of 32, so 100 C returns 210 instead of 212.
Delta conversions apply the absolute-temperature offset, so a 10 C delta returns 50 instead of 18.
The absolute-zero check also applies to deltas, so a large negative delta fails with BelowAbsoluteZero.
faults.find: if (!delta && quantity < ABSOLUTE_ZERO[from as "C" | "F"]) throw new BelowAbsoluteZero();
faults.replace: if (quantity < ABSOLUTE_ZERO[from as "C" | "F"]) throw new BelowAbsoluteZero();

statement: Each successful conversion sends exactly one entry to the sink, carrying the category, source unit, target unit, input quantity, rounded result and a timestamp from the sink's own clock.

faults.description: The rounded result is dropped from the entry sent to the sink.
faults.replace: await write({ category: entry.category, from: entry.from, to: entry.to, quantity: entry.quantity, timestamp: now() } as never);

faults.description: The timestamp comes from Date.now() instead of the sink's own clock.
A successful audit call writes the entry to the sink a second time, so one conversion produces two entries.
faults.replace:
await write({ ...entry, timestamp: now() });
    return undefined;

statement: The scaler applies the multiplier first and converts afterwards, and a scale factor of zero or less fails with InvalidScale.

faults.description: The ingredient quantity is multiplied by itself instead of by the scale factor, so the requested scaling is ignored.
A scale factor of exactly zero is accepted instead of failing with InvalidScale, and every ingredient scales to 0.

statement: Every conversion the scaler performs goes through the registry and the audit log, giving one entry per converted ingredient and none for ingredients already in the target unit.

faults.description: Ingredients already in the target unit are no longer skipped, so they go through the registry and produce an audit entry.
The registry no longer calls the audit component, so scaler conversions leave no log entry.
faults.find: const warning = await record({ category, from, to, quantity: quantity as number, result });
faults.replace: const warning = undefined as AuditWriteFailed | undefined;
